Third-party stores are off. A store serves its own copies of apps, not files from the developer\'s own site, and Tern reads it through the interface the store made for its own app or website. With them on, Tern asks a store only for the apps you add from it, and until an app is pinned to a certificate, the first file Tern installs from a store decides which certificate its updates must carry.

Third-party stores

APKPure, Aptoide, APKCombo, APKMirror, Tencent, Huawei AppGallery, the Galaxy Store and vivo. They serve their own copies of apps, not files from the developer\'s own site, and Tern reads them through the interfaces they made for their own apps and websites. Off, Tern asks none of them anything, a search leaves them out and apps from them are paused.
off in Settings
The file matches the store\'s checksum

A checksum is a fingerprint of the file itself. The store gave one, and the file Tern downloaded has the same, so it arrived as the store has it. The store is not the developer, so this says nothing about who made the file. The certificate does.

These come from third-party stores, which serve their own copies of apps. Until an app is pinned to a certificate, the first file Tern installs from its store decides which certificate its updates must carry.
Third-party stores are off, so these apps are paused. Tern asks those stores nothing until you turn them on.
